title: QA — what ran, and what it did
description: The executed record (SPEC §5 qa): every suite QA ran and every test it recognised, by the id the binding gave it. Nothing here is anyone's opinion — a suite either started or did not, a test either passed or did not, and both are read from output. The oracle's judgement on whether a criterion is discharged lives on the verdict, not here, so that what was observed and what it was taken to mean can be read apart. Hashed over the tests, so a verdict pinned to it goes stale when the suites are run again.

suites.description: One per suite QA knows how to run. `ok` is the runner's exit, `tests` how many titles it named. A suite that exits non-zero having produced no test the binding can join to did not run, which is a different thing from one whose tests failed — and the join, not the title count, is what says so: a runner handed a path it cannot load still prints one title naming that path.

command.description: What was run, verbatim, so a person can run it themselves.

tests.description: Every test the binding named that QA found in a suite's output, joined by the id carried in its title. An id the binding names and no title carries does not appear here — it is `test-missing` on the verdict, because a test that did not run must never be indistinguishable from one that passed.

passed.description: True only if every test carrying this id passed: one id driven by two tests is discharged by both or by neither.

unprovable.description: Tests the binding named that could not be walked here, with the environment names they were waiting on. Kept apart from `tests` because a test that did not run is not a test that failed, and a reader of the record is owed the difference: one says the product is wrong, the other says this machine could not ask.
